metadata.case_name: TSANG KAY PING ALIAS TSANG TING AND OTHERS v. LO WAI YU AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: sub-contractor in caisson work (digging mud and breaking rock)

injuries.description: fracture of the right scapula bone
source: "There were-multiple lacerations over the head, right shoulder and right side of the back. Abrasions were found over the right elbow, right leg, right shoulder and right side of the back. X-ray revealed fracture of the right scapula bone."

"(2) He suffered a fractured scapula which healed in good position. I believe that when Dr. Wedderburn wrote on 14th December 1977 that \"he should now have good movement of the. shoulder joint\" that is substantially what in fact he then enjoyed."
"X-rays were produced to Dr. Wedderburn, said to have been taken privately of the plaintiff, which revealed fractures of the 1st, 4th and 5th ribs."
"(3) He suffered three broken ribs which unhappily seem to have escaped notice in hospital."

injuries.description: multiple lacerations and abrasions (over the head, right shoulder, right side of the back; abrasions over right elbow, right leg, right shoulder and right side of the back)
injuries.body_part: head; right shoulder; right side of the back; right elbow; right leg
source: "There were-multiple lacerations over the head, right shoulder and right side of the back. Abrasions were found over the right elbow, right leg, right shoulder and right side of the back. X-ray revealed fracture of the right scapula bone."
"(4) He suffered the multiple lacerations and abrasions described in the hospital report."
injuries.icd_description: Multiple injuries of shoulder or upper arm

injuries.description: possible momentary concussion (no established brain damage)
source: "I am not satisfied that he suffered any brain damage in this accident. There is no sufficient connection on the evidence between this lesion and trauma, let alone this particular trauma. I am not satisfied of any head injury beyond lacerations, of anything more than possible momentary concussion, or of any amnesia."
"...which suggested both concussion and post-traumatic amnesia, Dr. Wedderburn feared some brain damage."

manifestations.description: serious loss of abduction in the right arm (right arm and shoulder joint moved as one; likened to almost complete ankylosis of the scapula to the humerus)
pain in the right shoulder on overuse
great pain over the right ribs and armpit much of the time
numbness on the right side of the body
dulled intellect and memory (claimed by plaintiff; attributed by some doctors to brain lesion)
pain and suffering from physical injuries and shock of the accident
flashes of bad-temper and irritation at his disability (no real personality change found)

treatments_received: Surgical toilet and suturing for the lacerations
admission to hospital (Surgical Ward A then Orthopaedic Ward)

losses.description: Loss of earnings and earning capacity: total loss of wages in 1977 for 7 months at $2,100 a month ($14,700) plus an additional allowance of $15,000 (total under this head $29,700).
Pain, suffering and loss of amenity awarded at $20,000.
Payments to herbalists and bonesetters allowed as special damage in the sum of $3,000.
anxiety neurosis flashes of bad-temper and irritation at his disability (no real personality change found)
